chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from some of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at al-Hira when a messenger of Abu Ja'far the Caliph came to him, summoning him. So he called for a raincoat, one side of which was black and the other white, and he wore it. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: But I am wearing it while I know that it is the clothing of the inhabitants of the Fire.

key_terms.الحيرة: Al-Hira, a historic city near Kufa in Iraq, used as a base by Abbasid Caliphs
key_terms.الخليفة: The Caliph — here referring to the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur (r. 136-158 AH)
key_terms.لباس أهل النار: The clothing of the inhabitants of the Fire — a phrase indicating the religious disapproval of black garments
key_terms.ممطر: A raincoat or cloak (mimtar), a reversible garment used in rain

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about wearing black clothing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was at al-Hira — a city near al-Kufa that served as a residence of the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur (Abu Ja'far) — when summoned to the Caliph's court. He donned a black-and-white reversible raincoat, a practical necessity for the occasion, while openly remarking to his companion Hudhayfa ibn Mansur that he knew it to be the garment of Hellfire's inhabitants. This statement reflects the Imam's principled disapproval of black garments, associated in Shia jurisprudential tradition with the Abbasids who mandated black as their dynastic color, while making clear he wore it only under political compulsion.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Hira, a messenger of Abu Ja’far the Caliph came over calling him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> called for the rain-coat, one aspect of it being black and the other white, so he<sup>asws</sup> wore it. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, I<sup>asws</sup> am wearing it and I<sup>asws</sup> know that it is a clothing of the inhabitants of the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from certain persons of his people from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhafah ibn Mansur who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in al-Hirah (a city in Iraq) when the messenger of abu Ja‘far al-Mansur, the caliph came to call him. He (the Imam) asked for a raincoat, one side black and the other side white, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I wear it but I know that it is the dress of the people of fire.”” (Black was the emblem of al-‘Abbaside rulers. Imam wore it due to Taqiyah (caution because of fear)
